summary: A first-ever Trump–Xi–Putin summit is planned for next week, Iran claims a strike on a US radar in Bahrain, and Russia and Ukraine agree a prisoner swap.

stories.headline: White House says Trump, Xi and Putin plan first three-way summit
stories.dek: It is planned for the APEC summit in China on 18–19 November, a US official says.
what: A senior US official said the talks will cover nuclear non-proliferation and the Iran war, not Ukraine. No new agreements are expected.
The Kremlin said earlier this month it was working to arrange it. Beijing has said only that it is in communication with the parties.
Kyiv says the summit would only encourage Putin to keep fighting. Germany's president says Europeans must be at the table on Ukraine.
background: Leaders of the US, Russia and China have never held a three-way summit. New START, the nuclear treaty between Washington and Moscow, expired in February 2026.
stories.why: Arms limits between the largest nuclear powers have lapsed. What the three leaders agree could affect the Iran war and Ukraine.
stories.say: Trump, Xi and Putin may meet in China next week, and Ukraine is officially off the agenda.

terms.def: Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation: a yearly summit of 21 Pacific-rim economies. China hosts this year, in Shenzhen.
Efforts to stop nuclear weapons spreading to more countries.

stories.headline: Iran claims strike on US radar in Bahrain; US says drones downed
stories.dek: Reuters calls it Iran's first claimed attack on US forces in a Gulf state since early September.
what: Iran's Revolutionary Guard says it destroyed a US early-warning radar in Bahrain on Friday, in revenge for a strike on a telecoms tower in southern Iran.
US Central Command says it shot down two Iranian attack drones, with no injuries or damage. Neither side's claim is independently confirmed.
Trump said on Thursday the US no longer needs a deal. Iran reportedly told the UN nuclear watchdog inspectors cannot return while Washington threatens it.
background: The war began on 28 February with US and Israeli attacks on Iran. The US now blockades Iranian ports, and shipping through the Strait of Hormuz has been disrupted.
stories.why: About a fifth of the world's oil passes through Hormuz. Wider fighting there can push up fuel prices everywhere.
stories.say: Iran says it hit a US radar. The US says it downed drones. Neither is confirmed.

terms.def: US Central Command, the American military headquarters covering the Middle East.
A cheap drone packed with explosives that crashes into its target.

stories.headline: Russia and Ukraine agree a big prisoner swap, but not on land
stories.dek: US envoys were due to brief Putin in Moscow, then meet Zelenskyy in Ireland.
what: The Abu Dhabi talks ended on 11 November with agreement in principle on a large prisoner swap. Numbers were due on Thursday.
US envoy Jared Kushner called territory the hardest issue and said the sides do not trust each other. Kyiv rejects Moscow's demand for all of Donbas.
Kyiv wants Europe at the next round. No date or venue has been set.
background: Russia invaded in February 2022. The front is largely stuck, and both sides keep striking each other's cities and power sites.
stories.why: A big swap brings relief to families, but with land unresolved, peace still looks far off.
stories.say: Russia and Ukraine agreed to swap prisoners but are still far apart on land.

terms.def: Ukraine's eastern Donetsk and Luhansk regions. Russia wants Kyiv to hand over all of it.

stories.headline: Israel's Eisenkot warns Netanyahu against new war while he builds a coalition
stories.dek: The former army chief says Israel should not return to war in the coming weeks.
what: Eisenkot says Israel should not resume fighting soon unless it faces an immediate threat. He says he has asked for operational updates and been refused.
Israeli media report the security cabinet has ordered preparations for a possible attack on Iran. Netanyahu's office says decisions are made solely for security reasons.
The Knesset convened on 10 November, and Eisenkot's allies agreed a first deal on parliamentary posts. A full coalition deal is expected to be harder.
background: Israel voted on 27 October. Eisenkot's alliance won 48 seats and Netanyahu's bloc 53. Neither has the 61 needed, and Eisenkot rules out a government with Arab-led parties.
stories.why: Whoever governs will decide Israel's next steps on Gaza and Iran, as the US and Iran trade threats.
stories.say: Eisenkot has the mandate to replace Netanyahu and is already warning him not to start a war.

terms.def: Israel's parliament, which has 120 seats. A coalition needs 61.

stories.headline: Democrat Scott Colom narrowly flips Republican-held Mississippi Senate seat
stories.dek: He is the state's first Black senator since Reconstruction, after more than a week of counting.
what: Colom beat Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith by 4,669 votes, according to Fox. The result was called on 11 November.
Early counts had the two just 65 votes apart. Mississippi has no runoff, so the top vote-getter wins.
No Democrat has represented Mississippi in the Senate since 1989.
background: The 3 November midterms were projected to hand Democrats control of Congress. Axios called Colom's win a stunning upset.
stories.why: Every Senate seat counts towards the majority that passes laws and confirms Trump's appointees.
stories.say: Mississippi just elected its first Democratic senator since 1989, and its first Black senator since Reconstruction.

terms.def: The years after the US Civil War when the South was rebuilt and Black men first held office.

stories.headline: Nvidia scandal pushes Congress toward tighter limits on chips to China
stories.dek: Three export bills may ride on the US defence bill as Nvidia searches for a new CEO.
what: Three bills tightening China's access to AI chips may be added to the 2027 defence bill, Reuters reports.
They would give Congress a say over chip exports, make firms track chips to stop smuggling, and push allies to restrict chipmaking equipment.
A former congressional staffer says Nvidia is the biggest opponent of two of them. Nvidia declined to comment. It reports earnings on 17 November.
background: Jensen Huang quit as Nvidia CEO on 12 November after a board probe into his relationship with a woman US intelligence reportedly suspects of working for Beijing. China denies it. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO.
stories.why: Nvidia makes most of the world's AI chips. Tighter US rules would shape who can build advanced AI, and how fast.
stories.say: Nvidia's scandal has given lawmakers a fresh reason to tighten the chip controls they were already pushing.

terms.def: The annual US defence spending law, often used to carry other national-security measures.

briefs.text: Asked about military action against Cuba on Thursday, Trump said he would like to be able to do it, per Drop Site News citing NBC. No plan has been reported.
Japan's PM Takaichi will attend APEC in Shenzhen on 18–19 November, but a formal meeting with Xi looks unlikely, Bloomberg reports. Ties are among their lowest since 1972.
Sudan's army and allied forces say they have captured Al-Khuwai and Serif Ankoush in West Kordofan from the RSF. Not independently confirmed.
